comment: Field notes: what this project has learned about a gate in its own tree (the fixture it trips on, the fix that is usually right). A note prints as one `FIELD-NOTE[<gate>]: <text>` line right after that gate's `FIX[<gate>]` line, and only when the gate fails; it never changes a verdict or an exit code, and it cannot hide a finding. Shape: {"notes": {"<gate>": "one string"}}. Key on the token printed in the FAIL line (`<gate>: FAIL`), which is the script's own gate name and not always its chain step's: the docs-sync step's scripts report as docs-sync, essential-eight and conformance-map, and check-framework-floor.mjs reports as floor-review. A key that does not match ^[a-z0-9-]+$, and a value that is not a string, are ignored. Whitespace collapses to single spaces, control and format characters are removed, and the text is capped at FIELD_NOTE_MAX_CHARS code points (tools/lib/gate.mjs). A step whose scripts never print a `<gate>: FAIL` line through tools/lib/gate.mjs (format, types, lint, dead-code, architecture, rls-isolation, unit, mobile-unit) gets no note. Write-guard-protected: the text reaches an agent while it is deciding how to make a red go away, so a human writes it and commits it. Seeded empty.
